- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior period), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in early forecast window (first 5–7 days); apply +0.8–1.2% bias to first 5 days if sentiment is neutral or positive.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive within 3–5 days, model lags in adjusting; forecast should rise 1–2% faster than historical mean reversion rate.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model tends to average or smooth out volatility; increase forecast volatility by 10–20% to match true price swings.
- If model consistently forecasts higher than true outcome in 3–5 consecutive days, apply downward correction of 0.5–1.0% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
